“Daredevil” star Charlie Cox says he was left flabbergasted over the response he received when he asked to audition to be the next James Bond in the franchise’s upcoming 26th installment.

Cox, 43, said in a Monday interview on Virgin Radio U.K.’s “The Chris Evans Breakfast Show” that he was told he was “too old” for the 007 role — even though 40-year-old Robert Pattinson landed the gig.

“Can I say something? I asked to audition for that,” Cox explained. “Do you know what they told me? ‘Too old.’ But Rob is the same age as me! He does look good for it, I have to be fair.”

Cox noted that he will be 44 in December, and questioned how that age is considered to be too old.

Amazon MGM Studios officially announced Pattinson as the next Bond on Nov. 16 after rumors briefly circulated he was in the running to take on the iconic role.

The unveiling came after years of speculation that actors Nicholas Hoult, Idris Elba, Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Aaron Taylor-Johnson and Josh O’Connor were being eyed for the role.

“I thought it was going to be Jack Lowden or maybe Callum Turner,” Cox admitted about the previously vacant role.

Cox praised Pattinson for his sweeping acting portfolio, which includes major films like “Dune: Part Three,” “The Odyssey” and “The Batman.”

“What an amazing career [Pattinson] has carved out. Some of the stuff that guy has done… worked with directors who have gone on to be huge, huge auteurs, but when he worked with them it was their first film or stuff.”

Before Pattinson, Daniel Craig portrayed the fictional British secret agent for 15 years, starring in five movies in the franchise. Craig’s final 007 movie was “No Time to Die” in 2021. Other actors who have played James Bond include Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton and Pierce Brosnan.

Pattinson’s James Bond film, directed by Denis Villeneuve, does not have an official release date yet, but could have a potential 2028 debut, according to People. Production for the movie is expected to begin in 2027.
